newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey undaunted by EU membership snub.
newsitem.headline: Turkey undaunted by EU membership snub.

text.p: Turkey was undaunted on Wednesday after a snub by European centrist politicians to its long-held ambitions for full membership of the European Union.

"Our message is the same. Turkey should be part of the extension of the EU. We have given this message before and we will give it again," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news conference.
Senior European politicians spoke out clearly against Turkey's membership at a meeting of the mainly Christian Democrat European People's Party (EPP) in Brussels on Tuesday.
But Ankara said it had not received the same message through official channels. "We have not been informed of such a stance by the EU. This meeting has to be assessed on its own," Atacanli said.
The meeting included German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

"It was unanimous against Turkish membership," Prodi told Italian reporters. But Christian Democrats still recommend closer ties with Turkey, a NATO member straddling the sensitive Balkans, Caucasus and Middle East.
Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller is to push Turkey's bid for membership at a lunch with the ambassadors of EU nations on Thursday, Atacanli said.
The EU has kept Turkey at arm's length because of Ankara's human rights record, economic troubles and disputes with member Greece.
